title: POST-HARVEST LOSS AND BYCATCH FROM MARINE FISHERIES
body_text:
The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) during the year 2023-24 carried out a comprehensive study through the National Productivity Council of India (NPC), an autonomous organization under Ministry of Commerce and Industry to assess post-harvest losses in fisheries and aquaculture sector. The study estimated post-harvest loss in marine fisheries in Karnataka between 6.21% to 10.13%.  Further, Government of Karnataka has also reported that as per the studies done by the ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Technology(CIFT) the estimated post-harvest loss is around 6%. It is also reported by Government of Karnataka that as per the studies done by the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) the bycatch was reported around 20-40% based on the type of gear and craft used in marine fisheries.
The DoF, GoI, under its schemes and policy accords high priory towards strengthening cold chain facilities, reduction of bycatch and efficient utilization of fish harvested. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), implemented by the DoF, GoI envisages support towards creation and modernization of post-harvest and cold chain infrastructure to reduce post-harvest losses, improve value realization, enhance shelf life of fishes harvested. The DoF, GoI encourages adoption of sustainable measures to minimize marine bycatch. Concurrently, States/Union Territories (UTs) are also encouraged towards optimal and value-added utilization of all harvested resources, thereby reducing post-harvest losses and promoting a circular economy in the fisheries sector.
During last five years and current financial year (FY 2026-27) under PMMSY, the DoF, GoI has accorded approval to the fisheries development proposals of Government of Karnataka with a total project cost amounting to ₹ 1053.60 crore. The approved activities inter-alia also included cold chain facilities like establishment of Ice plants/cold storages (126 units.), post-harvest transportation units (1065 units) which included refrigerated vehicles, insulated vehicles, motor cycle with ice boxes, cycle with ice boxes, three wheelers with ice boxes etc.,  live fish vending centres (46 units), fish kiosks (100 units), fish retail market (1 unit), matsya vahini mobile eco-friendly fish kiosks (300 units) and state of art whole sale fish market (1 unit). Under PMMSY, identification and selection of beneficiaries are carried out by the respective State Governments. The Government of Karnataka has informed that 171 beneficiaries have been supported under the cold chain infrastructure component of PMMSY.
Under PMMSY, the DoF, GoI has approved modernization and upgradation of Mangaluru Fishing Harbour at project cost of ₹ 37.47 crore which envisages improved berthing facilities, modern fish landing and auction infrastructure, hygienic fish handling areas, upgraded water supply, sanitation and waste management facilities, and upgraded harbour utilities to minimize handling losses and improve fish quality. In addition, in the adjoining areas projects namely modernization of Gangolli Fishing Harbour (₹ 22.18 crore) and Malpe Fishing Harbour (₹ 12.52 crore) has also been approved for providing similar facilities. Government of Karnataka has also informed that fishermen are encouraged to use Square-mesh cod-end trawl nets (35 mm) to allow juveniles to escape, and to install Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) in trawl nets to allow turtles to escape; both measures aimed towards conservation and sustainable fisheries.
This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked.

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) stated that studies by NPC and ICAR-CIFT estimate post-harvest losses in Karnataka's marine fisheries at around 6-10%, while ICAR-CMFRI found bycatch levels of 20-40% depending on gear and craft type. Under PMMSY, the DoF has approved ₹1053.60 crore worth of fisheries development projects for Karnataka over the last five years and FY 2026-27, including cold chain infrastructure (ice plants, cold storages, transport units, fish kiosks) benefiting 171 beneficiaries. Additionally, modernization of Mangaluru, Gangolli, and Malpe fishing harbours has been approved, and Karnataka promotes square-mesh cod-end trawl nets and Turtle Excluder Devices for sustainable fishing.
enrichment.context:
Post-harvest losses and bycatch are longstanding challenges in India's marine fisheries sector, affecting fishermen's incomes, food security, and marine biodiversity. Post-harvest losses occur due to inadequate cold chain infrastructure, poor handling, and transportation delays, while bycatch—the unintended capture of non-target species including juveniles and endangered species like turtles—threatens sustainable fish stocks and marine ecosystems. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), launched in 2020 as India's flagship fisheries scheme with an outlay of over ₹20,000 crore, aims to double fish exports, enhance productivity, and modernize the value chain from harvest to market, including cold storage and post-harvest infrastructure. This complements India's Blue Economy vision and the broader push for a circular economy in fisheries to minimize waste and maximize value addition.

Bycatch reduction measures like Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) and square-mesh cod-end nets are part of India's compliance with international conservation norms, given that Olive Ridley turtles nesting along the Indian coast are protected under the Wildlife Protection Act and various international agreements. Karnataka, with its significant coastline (Mangaluru, Malpe, Gangolli harbours), is a key marine fishing state, and harbour modernization projects here reflect the government's efforts to build world-class fishing infrastructure to reduce spoilage and improve hygiene standards, aligning with export competitiveness goals under initiatives like the Sagarmala programme and India's seafood export ambitions.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is implemented by which of the following ministries?
options: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
prelims_questions.explanation: PMMSY is implemented by the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, as stated in the release.

prelims_questions.question: Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs), mentioned in context of Karnataka's marine fisheries, are primarily used to:
options: Increase the catch of commercially valuable fish species
Allow sea turtles to escape from trawl nets, preventing accidental capture
Detect fish shoals using sonar technology
prelims_questions.explanation: TEDs are installed in trawl nets specifically to allow turtles, which may get accidentally caught as bycatch, to escape and avoid injury or death, aiding marine conservation.

mains_questions.question: Post-harvest losses and bycatch remain significant challenges in India's marine fisheries sector. Discuss the causes of these issues and evaluate the effectiveness of government schemes like PMMSY in addressing them.

mains_questions.question: Sustainable fishing practices are essential for balancing economic livelihoods with marine biodiversity conservation. Discuss with reference to bycatch reduction technologies and their implementation challenges in India.
